_comment.DisableClusterFlattening: Set to true to stop ironing the terrain under a city flat and let the streets
follow it instead. Cities become genuinely three dimensional.
Streets, traffic, pedestrians, the player's car, the pavements and the ground
under them all follow the terrain. That half works.
UNFINISHED, and this is why it is still off by default: everything that STANDS
on that ground was written against a flat city and has not been revisited.
Buildings take one height for a footprint that is nearly the whole block, so
every one of them has a corner in the air and a corner underground. Half the
shop windows on a hillside end up below the pavement. Quest markers sink about
half a metre into the road. Intercity trams fly a straight line roughly 47 m up.
The pavement also tilts sideways as much as it does lengthwise, because a block
floor is one warped polygon with no interior vertices.
